title: Annotatio IV §.IV: Second argument — cup and broken bread communion (1 Cor. 10:16–17) is spiritual
pass_a_gloss: The Second Argument from the tenth chapter of the former Epistle to the Corinthians is taken from that Communion of the cup of blessing with Christ’s blood, and that communion of the broken bread with Christ’s body, which is like the communion and coalescence into one body of those who become partakers of the same Lord’s bread — or even of the one bread with the article, i.e. of the same spiritual bread, or of Christ the Lord Himself? So Christ at vv. 16–17: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? the bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? For we being many are one bread, one body: for we all partake of that one bread. But their Union into the same body and communion is not corporal, but Spiritual.
pass_b_english: Second argument (1 Cor. 10:16–17): communion of the cup of blessing with Christ’s blood and of the broken bread with His body is like coalescing into one body as partakers of the one spiritual bread — Christ Himself.
That union into one body is not corporal but Spiritual.
source_text: Alterum Argumentum ex decimo Capite prioris Epistolæ ad Corinthios, desumtum, ab ea Communione poculi benedictionis cum sanguine Christi, & ea communione panis fracti cum corpore Christi petitum est, quæ similis existit communioni & in unum corpus coalitiioni eorum, qui ejusdem panis Dominici, vel etiam tou henos artou cum articulo, i. e. ejusdem panis spiritualis, seu Christi Domini ipsius participes fiunt? Ita enim Christus vers. 16. & 17. Poculum benedictionis, cui benedicimus, nonne communicatio sanguinis Christi est? panis quem frangimus, nonne communicatio corporis Christi est? Nam unus est panis, unum corpus multi sumus: nam omnes ex eodem pane participamus. At horum Unio in idem corpus communioque, non est corporalis, sed Spiritualis.
